verdict: OK to lend in Aligarh fasteners & hardware — back the organised, export-linked and OEM-supplying units with tight structure; avoid the small lock/hardware units already showing stress.
title: Aligarh fasteners & hardware: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Aligarh is a lock-and-hardware cluster first, with fasteners riding the same metal-working base.** Units buy steel and zinc, stamp, cast, machine, plate and assemble, then sell to traders, OEMs and exporters [1]. Cash turns on the metal-to-dispatch cycle, not on brand. **Steel is the swing cost — rating work on a fastener peer puts raw material at 50–55% of operating cost [8], so when a proposal lands, check the steel procurement and pass-through clause before anything else; if there is no price-reimbursement agreement with key customers, ask how a steel spike is absorbed.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits with units that have a customer price clause and a testing/quality gate; cash sits with whoever gets paid before the trader does.** The cluster's locks are tested outside Aligarh, which adds lead time and cost [1]. Peer results show the money is in OEM and export books: Sundaram Fasteners grew revenue ~30% YoY with exports up 57% [5], and Sterling Tools posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue, up ~32% [4]. **So when a proposal lands, check the export/OEM share of sales; if it is trader-only domestic, ask for the top-five buyer list and their payment terms.**

## What has changed now
**The macro is supportive but the local stress is real.** UP GST collections rose 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and IIP for NIC 25 output is up 16.9% YoY [D]. Against that, local recovery practice flags locks & hardware among Aligarh's most stressed MSME segments [2]. Peer margins are being trimmed by steel and aluminium inflation — Sundaram's EBITDA margin came to 15.7% [7]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit is a stressed lock-maker or an organised fastener supplier; if the former, ask for the OTS/recovery history before sizing.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue organised fastener units supplying OEMs and exporters, and hardware traders with a Gulf buyer base [3].** Avoid sub-scale lock units with trader-only sales and a recovery file [2]. Structure as a working-capital line against stock and receivables, with a steel price-pass-through covenant and a monthly stock-and-debtor statement. **Take the GST return, bank statement and stock statement every month; if receivable days stretch beyond the stated terms, ask for the buyer-wise ageing.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch steel-cost absorption, export order flow and receivable ageing.** Peer export growth of 57% [5] and 40% H1 [5] shows demand exists; a unit losing export orders while steel rises is the one to exit. Rating work on a peer shows interest cover of 8.8x and debt/OPBDIT of 1.4x as the healthy benchmark [11]. **If a unit's cover slips toward half that, ask for a fresh CMA and reprice.**
watch: Filing gap or falling turnover vs stock -> ask for sales register and re-size the limit
Input cost up with no price clause -> seek customer pass-through proof or trim exposure
Days stretch beyond terms -> ask for buyer-wise ageing and top-five confirmation
Order book falls while peers grow -> review and consider exit
